title: 4 GO-TO-MARKET STRATEGIES EVERY FOUNDER SHOULD IMPLEMENT
excerpt: Why a GTM Strategy is Essential Every year, at least 50 million startups are launched globally. However, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, 20% fail within the first year,...
content:
Why a GTM Strategy is Essential

Every year, at least 50 million startups are launched globally. However, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, 20% fail within the first year, and 65% shut down within ten years. Despite this, many startups succeed because they have a solid Go-To-Market (GTM) strategy.

It’s not enough for a product or idea to solve a problem; it must also generate revenue to cover operational costs, turn a profit, and deliver returns on investment. That’s why a GTM strategy is essential before launching.

A GTM strategy is a structured framework for generating revenue after developing a product. Whether your startup is selling a product or providing a service, mapping out a GTM strategy is a key determinant of success.

Many founders make two major mistakes:

  1. Focusing too much on product development while neglecting marketing.
  2. Copying competitors instead of designing a targeted approach for their audience.

A well-defined GTM strategy ensures maximum product potential, speeds up market penetration, and increases the chances of success.

1. Identify Your Unique Value Proposition (UVP)

At the core of any product is its Main Value Proposition (MVP)—the essential function that makes it work. However, to successfully sell the product, a Unique Value Proposition (UVP) is needed.

Your UVP differentiates your product from competitors and provides a competitive advantage. It must:

  • Clearly define what the product does
  • Explain what problem it solves
  • Showcase how it solves the problem better than competitors

Your UVP should be visible across all marketing materials—from websites and ads to social media and pitch decks—to drive engagement and credibility. Knowing your UVP makes it easier to attract both customers and investors.

2. Define Your Target Audience

If you’re trying to sell anything, you must first know who you are selling to. This helps refine your sales pitch and ensures you target the right people.

Your target audience is the group of people most likely to buy your product. To define it, create an Ideal Customer Profile (ICP) by considering:

  • Demographics (age, gender, location, income)
  • Psychographics (interests, behaviors, values)
  • Pain Points (problems your product solves)
  • Buying Behavior (how they interact with similar products)

Once you create an ICP, conduct market research to verify if your ideal customer matches the actual market demand. Refining your audience helps in designing an effective marketing strategy.

3. Develop a Pricing Strategy

Your pricing model can determine your startup’s success. Whether you opt for one-time payments, subscriptions, or a freemium model, pricing must:

  • Be affordable for your target audience
  • Cover operational and production costs
  • Reflect on the value of your product

Market research on competitor pricing is essential, but undervaluing your product to undercut competitors can be a mistake. Instead, balance affordability and profitability while justifying your price with superior value.

4. Optimize Your Distribution & Marketing Funnel

If you don’t have a distribution and marketing plan, even the best product will struggle to gain traction. This step focuses on how to reach customers effectively.

Your marketing funnel should be guided by:

  • Your UVP – What makes your product unique?
  • Your Target Audience – Where do they spend their time?
  • Your Budget & KPIs – What channels deliver the best ROI?

Marketing Channels to Consider:

  • Social Media Ads (Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok)
  • SEO & Content Marketing (Blogs, YouTube, newsletters)
  • Influencer & Affiliate Marketing
  • Email & SMS Campaigns
  • Referral & Loyalty Programs

Choosing the right marketing funnel ensures you reach the right audience, convert leads into customers, and ultimately scale your business.

A Go-To-Market strategy is more than just a launch plan—it is a blueprint for sustained growth and scalability. By implementing these four essential GTM strategies, founders can:

  • Reach the right audience
  • Position their product effectively
  • Generate consistent revenue
  • Scale their business with confidence

title: The Zango: Amplifying Northern Nigeria’s innovation ecosystem
excerpt: While scrolling through social media, we came across Startup Zaria, an emerging platform in the heart of Zaria City, Kaduna State. This is yet another innovative addition to Northern Nigeria's...
content:
While scrolling through social media, we came across Startup Zaria, an emerging platform in the heart of Zaria City, Kaduna State. This is yet another innovative addition to Northern Nigeria’s growing tech scene. Over the past decade, the region has witnessed a remarkable increase in innovation, digital literacy, and technology adoption. However, despite this progress, Northern Nigeria continues to struggle with funding, infrastructure, and revenue generation. Why is that?

Innovation hubs such as CoLab in Kaduna, nHub in Jos, Startup Kano, and Kirkira Hub in Katsina have been instrumental in supporting tech entrepreneurs, mentoring aspiring founders, organizing accelerators, and even raising funds. Yet, these efforts have not been enough to position the region’s tech ecosystem on par with its southern counterpart, which continues to attract a disproportionate share of investment and attention.

The surge of tech startups solving diverse challenges in the region signals an abundance of untapped potential. However, despite their skills and innovative solutions, Northern talents struggle to compete on a national and global scale. The question remains: What is hindering the region’s growth, and why does the ecosystem lack the necessary structure and funding?

Despite the presence of innovation hubs, the region still lacks adequate resources and training. Access to world-class training and infrastructure is critical in harnessing skills and positioning talents on the global map. However, private entities, government bodies, and international partners are yet to provide sufficient support, leaving hubs and startups to do most of the heavy lifting with minimal investor backing.

Nigeria’s tech industry is heavily concentrated in the southern part of the country, and key players rarely extend their focus to the north. In today’s digital age, merely being talented or developing a product is not enough—there must be a structured pipeline to bring these innovations to market. Unfortunately, the Northern tech ecosystem remains fragmented, with no clear pathways for scaling products or securing employment opportunities for talented individuals.

For instance, many promising projects birthed from hackathons often stall at the prototype stage due to a lack of follow-up funding and structured market entry plans. The region does not necessarily need more innovation hubs; rather, it requires a well-defined pipeline to nurture startups, connect them to viable markets, and position them for sustainable growth.

In 2024, Nigerian startups raised over $400 million in funding. However, only a small fraction of this capital reached the Northern region—not due to a lack of talent or viable products but due to limited access to investors.

The common argument has been that Northern Nigeria’s tech community is still emerging, therefore, it lacks the exposure needed to attract funding. However, growth is impossible without investment. While international investors have become deeply entrenched in Nigeria’s tech ecosystem, only a handful of Northern startups meet their criteria for funding. Moreover, many indigenous investors continue to channel their resources into traditional sectors like oil and gas, rather than diversifying into technology. To catalyze growth, the region must shift its investment focus and create opportunities for local innovators.

When Northern investors actively support their own, it sets the stage for external investors to follow suit. By fostering a thriving ecosystem where innovators can develop and scale their solutions, the region will not only retain its talent but also attract new opportunities and partnerships.

Northern Nigeria is home to countless talented innovators solving real-world problems. However, these efforts need visibility and structured support to reach their full potential. This is where The Zango comes in.

We have created The Zango to shine a spotlight on the underreported tech and innovation sector in Northern Nigeria. Our mission is to provide startups in the region with the visibility they deserve, highlight the achievements of innovation hubs, and showcase the individuals driving change in the tech ecosystem. By amplifying these voices, we aim to bridge the gap between Northern innovators and the resources, funding, and recognition they need to compete on a national and global scale.

Support The Zango today and be part of the movement to make Northern Nigeria a formidable player in the tech ecosystem. Together, we can create the momentum needed for sustainable growth and development in the region.

Saratu Abubakar, a tech startup enthusiast and advocate for Northern Nigeria’s innovation ecosystem, is the Founder/Editor-In-Chief of The Zango and the Managing Editor of News Digest Nigeria. Through The Zango, she is committed to spotlighting the region’s tech landscape, bridging the gap between innovators and the opportunities they need to thrive. She can be reached on Saratu.abubakar@thezango.com
